text:
nina: Heads-up: thinking about adding a latency-driven auto-fallback that respects route quotas. Quick brain dump — want UX/API takeaways. Pinging @alex @sahil for platform + ops.

alex: Love it. Do you mean fallback decision if p99 latency > X for T secs? Need to decide: per-route vs per-service thresholds.

sahil: Be careful: if fallback bypasses quota checks it could blow customer committed capacity. We need penalty windows and a soft-latch to avoid flapping.

nina: Exactly. UX questions: how much surface in console? Options: "global default" toggle + per-route overrides, live preview + dry-run, historical audit. Which to ship first? :thinking: 

alex: Start with per-route overrides and a global default. Console should show "expected cost delta" when fallback path is used and a simple histogram of how often it would have fired historically.

maria: Telemetry must include decision_reason (latency|errors|quota), the p50/p95/p99 values at decision time, and a sample trace_id. We should sample full traces for ~1% of fallback events so SRE can root-cause.

ops-bot: system: prototype-autofallback triggered on staging at 2024-11-03T14:12Z — decisions=3, targets=[small-gpt, cached-response]. (auto-report)

kevin: Audit schema idea: immutable record with fields: actor (system/operator), policy_version, input_signals, decision_outcome, fallback_target_model, capacity_tier, and decision_id. Exportable as CSV + replay token for sandbox.

sahil: API debate: do we evaluate policy inline inside the router, or via a dedicated policy-eval service? Inline is lower latency but harder to simulate/dry-run. Policy-eval service is easier to version and replay but adds an extra network call.

alex: Proposal: policy-eval as a sidecar/cache service. Router asks for decision and caches the (input_hash -> decision) for TTL. Decision payload includes reason_code and ttl_ms. That keeps replayable audit and limits added latency.

nina: UX: console should show the exact "why" with a compact timeline — signals that crossed thresholds — and a "replay in sandbox" button that replays the same inputs against current candidate model(s). Also provide a one-click "snooze for 1h" for operators.

maria: Metrics to surface: histogram of latency delta (fallback_path_latency - primary_latency), cost delta, and false-positive tags (from manual feedback). Per-customer breakdown is important for reserved-capacity customers.

kevin: Retention/PII: audit records kept 90 days in hot store, archived to GCS for 2 years. Mask any prompt/response content and only keep model identifiers + a SHA256 prompt hash for diffs.

alex: Quick policy JSON sketch:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "auto-fallback-latency-v1",
  "enabled": true,
  "scope": "route",
  "thresholds": { "p99_ms": 1000, "duration_s": 30 },
  "cooldown_s": 300,
  "quota_behavior": "respect",
  "sampling": { "trace_sample_rate": 0.01 }
}
```

nina: Nice shape. Two UX knobs we should highlight in console: 1) "Preview mode" (show historical hits if enabled but do not actually route), 2) "Auto-apply after X days of stable signals" to reduce manual churn.

sahil: Also add a guard: if fallback would route to a cheaper model and customer is on Dedicated/reserved tier, require "respect" quota mode or explicit override approval.

maria: Add an operator feedback button on the audit pane: "This fallback was wrong" — tags the decision_id and routes to investigation queue.

kevin: For replay, generate a one-time replay token that the sandbox accepts; log token usage. Keep replay tokens short-lived and audit their usage.

nina: Sweet. Action items: alex to draft console mockups showing preview + audit pane, kevin to write audit schema + retention plan, maria to list telemetry fields and sampling plan, sahil to enumerate quota interactions and edgecases. I'll collect and we can iterate. :thumbsup:
